Condo buildings in Port Kells

Barnston Island isn't in Surrey: it's Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A plus Katzie First Nation reserve land. The real estate board files it under Port Kells only because the ferry lands at the foot of 104 Avenue in Port Kells.
Streets, schools and transit near Port Kells condos

items.t: Port Kells sits in the northeast corner of Surrey, on the south bank of the Fraser River, north and south of Highway 1, east of Highway 15 (176 Street), against the Langley border. It has two distinct halves: a large light-industrial district north of Highway 1, and a rural/low-density residential pocket ("South Port Kells") south of the highway. The City's economic arm profiles Port Kells as one of Surrey's major industrial areas (781 acres, roughly 610 businesses, mainly light industrial IL zoning).

Nearby areas: Tynehead and Fleetwood (west/southwest), Guildford (west), Walnut Grove in the Township of Langley (east), Anniedale-Tynehead (immediately south, Neighbourhood Concept Plan in preparation).

There are no condos in Port Kells. Homes are mostly freehold detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots, plus cluster housing shown in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan. North of Highway 1 it's industrial, not housing.

Schools: Port Kells Elementary (K–7) at 19076 88 Avenue, School District 36 (Surrey); the current school building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places. A School Locator check for 19076 88 Avenue returned Port Kells Elementary and Ecole Salish Secondary. Catchments are address-based — confirm other addresses in the locator.

Highway 1, Highway 15 (south to the U.S. commercial border crossing) and Highway 17 / South Fraser Way run through or beside the area. The Barnston Island Ferry (free, provincial inland ferry, roughly 5-minute on-demand crossing, capacity ~6 vehicles) departs from the foot of 104 Avenue across Parson's Channel.

Recreation and shopping: no civic recreation centre and no retail centre in Port Kells itself; Tynehead Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) borders the area to the west, and the nearest full shopping is in Guildford and Langley's Walnut Grove.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Port Kells

items.t: Plans and zoning: Surrey's current Official Community Plan is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026). The area is also guided by the South Port Kells Land Use Plan, and North Port Kells is mostly zoned light industrial (IL). Surrey charges its own development cost charges for Port Kells industrial and commercial land, separate from city-wide rates, which matters if you plan to develop.

ALR rules govern the south pocket's farm parcels: the South Port Kells plan maps ALR boundary lands through the residential pocket; ALR status changes what a buyer can build, and ALC housing rules generally allow one residence per parcel (principal residence 500 m² or less, secondary suite only inside the principal residence). Check the ALR boundary on any south-side parcel before pricing in a second dwelling.

Surrey suites rule: a secondary suite in Surrey is capped at 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area — the suite rule that applies if a South Port Kells house (or any Surrey house a buyer chooses instead of a condo) is bought with suite income in mind; ALR parcels follow the ALC rule above instead.

blocks.text: Good to know about Port Kells condos

items.t: One name, two unrelated markets, split by a highway. North of Highway 1: an IL-zoned industrial district with its own DCC schedule and roughly 610 businesses. South of it: a rural-residential pocket under a separate adopted land use plan, with ALR parcels woven through it. A "Port Kells" search has to be split by highway side before it means anything.

The school is a heritage building. Port Kells Elementary's current building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places — the old village core around 88 Avenue is the residential pocket's historic centre, in a sub-area otherwise defined by warehouses.
Surrey replaced its OCP in 2026. Surrey 2050, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026), is the current plan — packages and older guides citing Bylaw 18020 are citing a superseded bylaw.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Port Kells
Streets, schools and transit near Port Kells townhomes

items.t: The residential stock is single-detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots plus cluster housing shown in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan, predominantly freehold; north of Highway 1 the land is industrial buildings, not housing.

Schools (SD36): Port Kells Elementary (K–7), 19076 88 Avenue, serves the area. Its building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places. Catchments are set by address, so check a specific home with the school district.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Port Kells

items.t: I don't know of any strata homes in Port Kells today, but for any strata purchase, including in nearby Guildford or Fleetwood, read the Form B. It shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
A fee-simple home carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees; municipal rules (Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000) plus any registered covenants or homeowners' association govern instead.

Agricultural Land Reserve land runs through South Port Kells. ALR homes can't be stratified. On ALR land, the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is only allowed inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. Check whether a south-side property is in the ALR before counting on a second home.

Secondary suites (Surrey, off-ALR parcels): one secondary suite may be permitted in a single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, one per unit, not a separate strata lot, and never inside a coach house or garden suite. ALR parcels follow the ALC rule above instead.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Port Kells
North Port Kells

items.t: North Port Kells is mostly light industrial: the City profiles it as one of Surrey's major industrial areas, with about 610 businesses across 781 acres, mainly manufacturing, construction and wholesale. It's warehouses, work yards and industrial buildings, not housing.

Port Kells-specific DCCs: Surrey publishes Port Kells-specific Development Cost Charges (2025 Port Kells Industrial DCCs and Commercial DCCs, listed separately from city-wide rates) — a real line item in any industrial land purchase with development intent, confirmed early in a pro forma.
Servicing, as stated: the industrial district is City-serviced employment land on the City profile.

blocks.text: South Port Kells

items.t: Homes are concentrated in South Port Kells: detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots, plus areas planned for cluster housing in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan. "Cluster housing" is a plan designation, not an existing complex or lots for sale.
Lot sizes: standard suburban lots to multi-acre rural/ALR parcels in the south pocket.
Tenure: The old village core around Port Kells Elementary (the school dates to 1907) carries mixed older stock with newer suburban builds at the edges.
Serviced vs unserviced: parcel-level servicing (municipal water/sewer vs well/septic) on the rural south side is not stated parcel by parcel.

blocks.text: Assemblies / plan ground

items.t: Anniedale-Tynehead, immediately south: a Neighbourhood Concept Plan now in preparation, planned for a mix of industrial, commercial and residential growth, which the City expects to increase land availability next to Port Kells. That is plan ground in preparation — it will change traffic, servicing and land values on Port Kells' south edge as it advances, but no part of it is a current lot offering documented here.
Barnston Island ground is not documented here

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Port Kells

items.t: City plan and zoning: Area-level guidance is the adopted South Port Kells Land Use Plan; North Port Kells is primarily light industrial (IL) zoning under Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.

Small-scale housing in Surrey (since July 8, 2024): up to 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, for eligible lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary. These rules don't override ALR status on farmland, and they don't legalize a suite or coach house built without permits.

Streamside setbacks: Surrey's streamside setbacks sit in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, varying by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated for a Port Kells parcel; the applicable setback is read off Part 7A for the watercourse class on the specific lot.

ALR residences cannot be stratified. ALC residence caps: principal residence ≤500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; an additional residence of 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² or less on parcels over 40 ha, under the ALC's rules or with approval. Check the ALR boundary on any south-side parcel before pricing.

A bare-land strata lot is strata ownership: BC strata rules apply, so check the Form B, depreciation report and contingency reserve, and note that rental bans are void and only 55+ age bylaws are valid. On ALR land, homes can't be stratified at all.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Port Kells?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 3 houses listed in Port Kells. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Port Kells from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 0 houses and 0 condos and townhomes sold in Port Kells over those 5 months.

faq.q: How big is Port Kells compared with the rest of Surrey?
faq.a: In October 2026, Port Kells held 0.3% of the 1,033 detached houses listed in Surrey.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Port Kells than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was 2 in June and 3 in October 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.

faq.q: Is there a condo or townhome I can buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: None that I know of. A buyer set on strata product is shopping Guildford, Fleetwood or Walnut Grove, not Port Kells. SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.

faq.q: What CAN I buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: A freehold house in South Port Kells (suburban lots to multi-acre rural/ALR parcels) or, north of Highway 1, an industrial property. The two markets share a name and almost nothing else.

faq.q: Is Port Kells really a board sub-area, or just an industrial park name?
faq.a: Port Kells is one of the real estate board's areas, and the City profiles it as a major industrial area. It isn't one of Surrey's six town centres.

faq.q: Is Barnston Island part of Port Kells / Surrey?
faq.a: No. Barnston Island is Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A plus Katzie IR 3 — it only codes to Port Kells for board purposes because the free ferry to it sails from the foot of 104 Avenue in Port Kells. Do not price or describe an island property as Surrey stock.

faq.q: Can I build a suite or second home on a South Port Kells acreage?
faq.a: It depends on zoning and, critically, ALR status: the land use plan shows ALR lands inside the residential pocket, and ALR parcels carry the ALC's residence limits (secondary suite only inside the principal residence). Off-ALR, Surrey's suite cap is 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area. Confirm both before pricing in a second dwelling.

faq.q: Is there a townhouse I can buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: No known one — of either tenure. A buyer set on townhouse product is shopping Guildford, Fleetwood or Walnut Grove, not Port Kells.

faq.q: What CAN I buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: A freehold house in South Port Kells (suburban lots to multi-acre rural/ALR parcels) or, north of Highway 1, an industrial property. The two markets share a name and almost nothing else.

faq.q: Is Port Kells really a board sub-area, or just an industrial park name?
faq.a: Port Kells is one of the real estate board's areas, and the City profiles it as a major industrial area. It isn't one of Surrey's six town centres; for planning, it's grouped with the Guildford area.

faq.q: A listing calls a Port Kells property a duplex — can I buy one side?
faq.a: Almost certainly not: Without a strata plan or a subdivided lot there is no separate half, and on ALR parcels residences cannot be stratified at all.

faq.q: Is Barnston Island part of Port Kells for a purchase?
faq.a: No — the island is Electoral Area A plus Katzie IR 3, not Surrey; it only codes to Port Kells in board data because the ferry lands here.

faq.q: The land use plan shows "cluster housing" in South Port Kells — is that duplex stock?
faq.a: No — it is a plan designation for the residential pocket, not a named complex.
